title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
summary: 1.6.0 ships instant XML↔Kotlin string resource navigation via a pre-built index and fixes KDoc hover at declaration sites.

highlights.title: O(1) String Resource Navigation
highlights.description: Jumps between R.string.* references and their XML definitions are now instant — a pre-built index replaces per-navigation file scanning.

highlights.title: KDoc Hover Accuracy
highlights.description: Hover documentation no longer appears at a symbol's own declaration site, and inherited KDoc from base methods is now resolved correctly.

highlights.title: Adversarial Test Coverage
highlights.description: New edge-case test suites for navigation providers, hover, and the resource index increase confidence in correct behavior across malformed and unusual inputs.

sections.heading: Improvements
bullets: Replaced per-navigation file scanning with a pre-built RResourceIndex, making jumps from R.string.* references to their XML definitions — and back — instant regardless of how many resource files the project contains.
Added two-way string resource navigation: jump from an R.string.* reference in Kotlin or Java to its XML definition, and from an XML string entry back to all Kotlin and Java usages.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Suppressed KDoc hover at a symbol's own declaration site, where it was redundant and visually noisy.
Fixed base method lookup depth in KDoc resolution — hover now correctly surfaces inherited documentation from the nearest supertype rather than stopping prematurely.

sections.heading: Notes
bullets: Added adversarial test suites covering navigation providers, the hover provider, and the resource index — these are internal but directly increase confidence that navigation results remain correct across malformed inputs and edge conditions.
